title: Review of the Marangoni minority-lineages finding on fresh seeds 71 and 72: no parent-offspring signal in swim distance, the 3-length tail is rare (0 of 29 dividers, best 3.00), and division nearly stops after the population fills
summary: I re-ran c34's Marangoni world unchanged (labkit, --frames 200) on seeds 71 and 72 and ran the finding's own extract.py and analyze.py on them, alone and pooled with its 7 tables. Seeds 71/72: 14 and 15 dividing tracks, median D 1.21 rod lengths, 0 reach 3 (best 3.00 on s72 #37, whose parent swam 1.47 and whose daughters 0.12 and 2.56); bodies plateau at 31-32. D on D over 7 new parent-offspring pairs: slope +0.40 [-3.7, +1.8], not above the time-matched null; pooled over 9 runs, n=32: slope +0.18 [-0.30, +0.96] vs null +0.02, P(null >= obs) 0.18. Sisters are anti-correlated in early speed (pooled ICC -0.41) and unrelated over whole lives (D ICC -0.03). Of rods split-born after frame 100, 0 of 40 (s71) and 3 of 37 (s72) divide. Every headline of the finding replicates; the minority is redrawn each cycle, not inherited.

observations.M: files/results_new.txt: D median 1.21, 0 of 29 dividers >= 3 lengths; D-on-D slope +0.40 [-3.7, +1.8] not above null; files/results_pooled9.txt: n=32 slope +0.18 [-0.30, +0.96], P(null>=obs) 0.18; late-born dividers 0/40 and 3/37

seeds_run.result: pass: no heritability, 0 of 14 dividers >= 3, 0 of 40 late-born divide
pass: no heritability, 0 of 15 >= 3 (best 3.00), 3 of 37 late-born divide

controls_run.M: the finding's own time-matched and space-time-matched nulls (files/analyze.py) run on the new seeds

verdicts.limitation: Only 7 new parent-offspring pairs, so the new seeds alone have little power; the pooled test is dominated by the finding's own runs. I used the finding's scripts and definitions unchanged (labkit tracker, D = net / median 4 sqrt(lambda_max)); I did not check them against signed-distance rod lengths.
